title: Thermal limits & germination rate
brief: Create a photorealistic Cannabis achene germination laboratory panel showing identical seed lots across a temperature gradient. Plot final germination percentage separately from germination rate, with radicle-emergence timing strips and a clear note that published cardinal temperatures are cultivar-, lot-, and method-specific rather than universal species constants.

title: Water potential, salinity & osmotic stress
brief: Create a seed-to-radicle cutaway showing water movement from the external solution through the pericarp and seed tissues under progressively lower water potential and increasing salinity. Pair realistic seed stages with a restrained osmotic-gradient overlay; do not imply one universal salinity threshold for Cannabis.

title: Seed vigor, aging & storage
brief: Create a scientific storage matrix comparing Cannabis seed moisture, temperature, storage time, and initial lot quality. Show viable-high-vigor, viable-low-vigor, and nonviable outcomes using germination speed, uniformity, and seedling establishment—not seed color alone. Avoid a universal shelf-life claim.

title: Pericarp resistance, priming & low-vigor germination
brief: Create a controlled comparison of intact Cannabis achenes, experimentally opened or pericarp-altered achenes, and primed low-vigor lots. Show emergence speed and uniformity as study-dependent outcomes and explicitly label priming or pericarp manipulation as context-dependent experimental interventions, not guaranteed rescue methods.

title: Root tip zones & apical growth
brief: Create a photorealistic longitudinal Cannabis root-tip cutaway from root cap through apical meristem, elongation zone, differentiation zone, and emerging root hairs. Use cellular scale transitions and restrained labels; distinguish Cannabis-specific anatomy from general vascular-plant developmental mechanisms.

title: Lateral root initiation & architecture plasticity
brief: Create a two-scale visual: microscope cutaway of lateral-root initiation inside the parent root, then a whole-root 3D comparison of contrasting hemp architectures. Emphasize genotype and growth-system variation in root length, lateral allocation, shape, and root-shoot biomass rather than one universal Cannabis root blueprint.

title: Radial water transport & aquaporins
brief: Create a root cross-section tracing water from rhizosphere through epidermis, cortex, endodermal region, and into xylem. Distinguish apoplastic and cell-to-cell pathways and show aquaporins as regulated membrane channels, never as pumps. Mark general plant mechanisms separately where Cannabis-specific flux measurements are unavailable.

title: Root microbiome, exudates & mycorrhizal interfaces
brief: Create a realistic Cannabis root and rhizosphere scene showing exudate release, rhizosphere and endosphere microbial communities, and an arbuscular-mycorrhizal interface. Encode associations as context-dependent interactions influenced by genotype, substrate, environment, inoculum, and management; do not depict all microbes as beneficial.

title: Sex chromosomes & early gene regulation
brief: Create a scientific XX/XY Cannabis reproductive-development timeline linking chromosome context to early sex-linked and sex-biased gene regulation before visible floral differentiation. Include current X-linked ethylene-pathway evidence while avoiding a simplistic single master-gene or active-Y explanation for every sex-expression outcome.

title: Ethylene-mediated sexual plasticity
brief: Create a split-panel model separating fixed chromosome complement from hormone-responsive floral phenotype. Show XX and XY Cannabis examples with ethylene signaling modulation affecting reproductive morphology while the chromosomes remain unchanged. Keep environmental and developmental modifiers visible as context.

title: Anther maturity, dehiscence & pollen release
brief: Create a photorealistic microscope sequence from developing Cannabis anther through mature pollen, longitudinal stomium opening, dehiscence, and pollen release. Use developmental stage rather than a fixed day or node number and clearly distinguish anther tissue from pollen grains.

title: Pollen viability, germination & storage
brief: Create a laboratory comparison showing freshly collected Cannabis pollen, non-abortion or staining observations, actual in-vitro pollen germination, and stored samples under contrasting moisture/temperature conditions. Make clear that intact-looking pollen is not equivalent to demonstrated germination capacity and that stored pollen requires viability testing.

title: CO2 diffusion & photosynthetic response
brief: Create an interactive leaf-atmosphere 3D overlay tracing CO2 from bulk air through the boundary layer and stomata into mesophyll while simultaneously showing PPFD, leaf temperature, stomatal conductance, photosynthesis, and transpiration. Present CO2 as one coupled input rather than an isolated universal target.

title: PPFD, DLI & photoperiod
brief: Create a clean scientific dashboard comparing instantaneous PPFD, integrated DLI, and photoperiod/nightlength using matched light schedules. Show that similar daily photon totals can arise from different intensity-duration combinations while photoperiod remains a separate developmental signal.

title: Light acclimation & canopy position
brief: Create a full-canopy Cannabis light map with upper, middle, and lower leaves linked to representative gas-exchange response panels. Show local light history and acclimation without implying one top-leaf measurement predicts whole-plant yield or flower chemistry.

title: Coupled environmental limits
brief: Create an interactive whole-plant limitation network connecting light, CO2, temperature, VPD, airflow, root-zone water, oxygen, and nutrient supply. Highlight how increasing one resource can shift the limiting process elsewhere. Avoid universal optimal setpoints and linear-response assumptions.

title: Nutrient symptom progression & tissue analysis
brief: Create a Cannabis diagnostic panel pairing old-versus-new and upper-versus-lower symptom progression with representative tissue-analysis results. Emphasize overlap among visual patterns, timing, antagonisms, developmental stage, and analytical evidence rather than treating one leaf photo or concentration threshold as definitive.

title: Root & crown: biotic vs abiotic clues
brief: Create a side-by-side root-and-crown differential showing healthy roots, waterlogging/low-oxygen stress, and representative pathogen-associated lesions or root loss. Include irrigation history, oxygen context, odor/texture observations, microscopy, and confirmatory testing cues; do not diagnose disease from brown roots alone.

title: Senescence vs disorder
brief: Create a developmental comparison between expected age- or flowering-associated senescence and atypical decline. Use distribution, rate of progression, developmental stage, root-zone/environment history, and healthy comparison plants as evidence layers rather than declaring all late-flower yellowing normal.

title: Evidence weighting & confirmatory testing
brief: Create an observation-to-diagnosis workflow in which a visual pattern generates multiple hypotheses, evidence is ranked by specificity and reliability, and the next discriminating measurement, microscopy check, tissue analysis, or molecular pathogen assay narrows the differential. Visually separate hypothesis, evidence, and confirmed diagnosis.
